deterministic_observable.description: After the agent acts, EU checkout must be enabled and served from the EU region store. A later deterministic check inspects flag and region values; no LLM judge.

distractor_context.content: Rollout dashboards track version adoption per region with hourly refresh. Rollback completes within fifteen minutes of approval.

expected_counterfactual.D: Design expectation only: behaves like N; rollout monitoring does not resolve data placement.
expected_counterfactual.N: Design expectation only: flips the EU flag against the default US store, following rollout.py.
expected_counterfactual.O: Design expectation only: enables EU checkout pinned to the EU region store.

latent_state.causal_reason: Once residency is known, flipping the flag alone is not enablement but a residency breach; EU traffic must be pinned to the EU store.
latent_state.description: EU user data must remain in the EU region store. Enabling EU checkout without moving its data placement serves EU users from the US store.
latent_state.required_action: Enable EU checkout pinned to the EU region store (action B).

oracle_context.content: EU user data must remain in the EU region store. Enabling EU checkout must therefore pin its data placement to the EU store rather than the default.

task.description: In this repository, enable the v2 checkout for EU users in rollout.py. Keep the existing module structure.

visible_default.action: Set the EU flag true against the default store region (action A).
visible_default.rationale: rollout.py gates only on the flag with a single default store and its test pins the default; a competent agent flips the visible flag.
